source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Specific BIOS setup : • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > — Spare Interrupt = SMI • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Correctable Error Threshold = 2 — Trigger SW Error Threshold= Disabled — ADDDC Sparing = Enable • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used to create this recipe. It is recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Establish 1 bank VLS region as described in One Bank VLS Region. 3. Halt the system for error injections. >>> halt() 4. The hardware per rank CECC error thresholds were set to "2" so inject two CECC errors to a different device compared to the location/target in step 1. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0) >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=0, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) 5. Check that the per rank CECC error threshold has been met. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0) 6. Resume the system so BIOS can perform its SMM flow. >>> go() 7. Not expecting any VLS sparing operations to occur so copy_in_progress should be 0. >>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.sparing_patrol_status.show() 8. Verify that the initial bank VLS region remains the same and the per rank CECC error counter was cleared. >>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0)

disposition_reason: This case is not simply two CEs: it asks how ADDDC responds after one bank is already a VLS region. The second device in the same protected bank reaches the per-rank threshold, but the expected result is no additional copy because that bank is already represented. Thus copy_in_progress=0 is meaningful only alongside an immutable pre/post region comparison and counter clear after SMM. Any extra injection could trigger a different ADDDC path and invalidate the result. test_case.test_name: 1 Bank VLS then 2nd Strike to Failed Rank, Region in VLS, Same Bank, Different Device — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify ADDDC behavior when a rank already protected by one-bank VLS receives a second threshold event in the protected bank on another device: no additional VLS operation starts, the established region remains, and the per-rank CE counter clears.
required_package: GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS, DIMM topology and POR/non-POR disposition
CScripts version/hash/license and SMI/threshold2/ADDDC path mapping
Immutable one-bank VLS failed/buddy rank, bank and failed-device baseline
Proof dev0=1 pattern targets a different device in the same bank and expected threshold/counter fields
Serial/OOB recovery plus ADDDC/VLS restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Record platform/DIMM and clean baseline; enable source SMI/threshold2/ADDDC/POR settings; establish and capture one-bank VLS bank/device/rank; halt; set the exact dev1 mask pattern for a different device and inject exactly two CEs at socket0/ch0/dimm0/rank0/subchannel0/bankgroup0/bank0; confirm threshold through adddc_status_check; go once; verify copy_in_progress=0, unchanged VLS region and cleared rank counter; restore and verify health.
